decisions.reason: As a safety shoe line in the firm's core protective-footwear domain, it draws on strong existing design, production, certification, and sales knowledge, so management would more likely refine it than withdraw it.

The supportive insole remains related to the firm's footwear knowledge base, but as a non-core add-on in a category already rationalised by dropping Product B, it is still somewhat exposed if it does not show a clear role alongside the flagship insole offer.
The ergonomic safety shoe series is highly consistent with the firm's accumulated know-how and visible innovation path, which makes continued improvement and retention more likely than exit.

Firefighter and rescue boots are a specialised but technologically adjacent extension of the firm's protective-footwear capabilities, so management would usually keep them unless niche demand and learning prospects disappoint.

Because the moulded insole was positioned as a flagship direction and fits closely with the firm's product-development and footwear expertise, management would be very unlikely to drop it and would instead keep investing in it.
